'''Richard Arnold Epstein''' (March 5, 1927 – July 5, 2016), also known under the pseudonym '''E. P. Stein''', was an American [[game theory|game theorist]].

==Early life and education==
Epstein was born in [[Los Angeles, California]]. He obtained his [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], in 1948. He then studied at the [[University of California Berkeley]]. He received his doctorate in [[physics]], on the [[Max Born|Born]] formalization of isochromatic lines, in 1961, from the [[University of Barcelona]].<ref>{{Cite journal |year=1964 |title=Contributors |journal=IEEE Transactions on Space Electronics and Telemetry |volume=10 |pages=47 |doi=10.1109/TSET.1964.4335592}}</ref>

==Career==
He then shifted from [[spectroscopy]] to space communications, and worked for eighteen years as an electronics and communications engineer for various U.S. space and missile programs. He was variously employed by [[Parsons-Aerojet Company]] at [[Cape Canaveral]], [[Glenn L. Martin Company]], [[TRW Inc.|TRW Space Technology Laboratories]], the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]], and [[Hughes Aircraft|Hughes Aircraft Space Systems Division]]. Epstein has numerous technical publications in the areas of [[probability theory]], [[statistics]], [[game theory]], and [[Outer space|space]] [[Telecommunication|communication]]s. In 1956, he was made a member of the [[IEEE]].

==Achievements==
''The Theory of Gambling and Statistical Logic'' ranks as the most popular of Epstein's technical books. He served as a consultant to public and private [[gambling]] [[casino]]s in [[Greece]] and [[Macao]], and he had testified on technical aspects of gambling in several court cases.

Under the pseudonym "E. P. Stein", he authored various popular works of fiction, as well as historic and non-fictional books, and wrote for TV and motion pictures.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Theory of Gambling |url=http://www.gamblingtheory.net/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819095601/http://www.gamblingtheory.net/index.html |archive-date=August 19, 2013 |access-date=August 19, 2013}}</ref>

==Death==
Epstein died on July 5, 2016.{{cn|date=June 2024}}
